passages.note: Wesco is listed as House sponsor of SB 101, Indiana's general RFRA.
Wesco voted Yea on House 3rd reading of SB 101.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text: general strict-scrutiny exemption, the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means test limits it.

rows.reasoning: Wesco was a House sponsor of SB 101 (2015) and voted Yea on its 3rd reading. The enrolled act is Indiana's general RFRA: it exempts a person's exercise of religion from substantial government burden unless the government shows a compelling interest and the least restrictive means, matching rung 4, 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs' (annex: a RFRA's strict-scrutiny test makes the exemption the default, limited by the compelling-interest test).
